title: PanelAlpha health check
description: One question asked of a deployed application's own response, and the sentence to say when the answer is wrong.

id.description: Unique within its group; also the filename. A stable identifier, not a label — telemetry counts these, so renaming one splits a check's history in two.

severity.description: `error` is an application a visitor cannot use. `warning` is one that works but is not what its author meant. Neither fails a deploy.

expect.description: What a healthy response looks like. Six keys, and no more: a question that needs to parse something other than JSON, read the disk or run a command belongs in `explain`, the way `detect` splits between its file rules and a named probe.

path.description: The local path to ask, `/` by default. A query string is allowed. A scheme, a host, or `//` is refused — the probe dials the application on loopback, and a check must not be able to send the engine elsewhere. Set it to ask an API where it states its own condition, instead of the page a browser would get.

status.description: Status codes that pass. Integers, or a class: 2xx, 3xx, 4xx, 5xx. Applies to the response for `path`.

body.description: Text that must appear in the response body.

body_not.description: Text that must not appear in the response body.

json.description: Members the body must contain, compared against the body parsed as JSON. Nested values are not supported — a claim about a document's shape belongs in an `explain` class. A member's value may be a list, read as "any of these"; numbers compare loosely, so 1.0 matches "1.0", while a boolean and the string "true" stay different answers.

when.description: A `detect` node gating this check, evaluated against the project by PlatformMatcher — the same guard a command carries. This is how one member of a group opts out of a check the group brings, without the manifests that opt out having to say so.

landing.description: Ask this check only when the probe, following redirects from `/`, ended under one of these paths (prefix match, query ignored). Any other landing passes. For a page that is only a problem where it lives, like an application's own installer.

message.description: One sentence a non-developer can act on, stating what is wrong. `{status}` interpolates the code that was returned.

fix.description: What to do about it, when that can be said without reading the project. An `explain` class overrides this with something specific.

serving.description: One word for what the application is serving instead of itself — `placeholder`, `missing_entry`. The first failing check that declares one names the report's `serving` field. A check the engine adds from outside the response, like the crash-loop one, declares it too.

explain.description: A named Explainer class that turns this failure into a diagnosis by reading the project. Runs only when the check has already failed, so a healthy application never pays for it.
